items.title: easyDNS Breach Exposes Customer Data and Unsalted Mailbox Password Hashes
items.summary: An attacker got into easyDNS’s Amazon Web Services account and took customer data, including mailbox password hashes the registrar never salted. CEO Mark Jeftovic disclosed the breach on the company blog on 27 November at 20:56 UTC. A day earlier, easyDNS had told customers who keep their own AWS keys in its control panel to rotate them immediately . easyDNS is a Canadian registrar and DNS host, founded in 1998. It says domains, DNS, email, SSL certificates and web forwarding kept working throughout. It hasn’t said how many customers are affected, or how the attacker got into its AWS account.

items.title: Flaw in Linux NFS file sharing exposes servers to remote takeover
items.summary: Researchers have found a critical flaw in the Linux kernel’s NFS file-sharing server that lets unauthenticated attackers obtain a root shell on affected systems. The flaw remained undetected in the kernel for 12 years, until two researchers, one using an AI agent, discovered it independently. NFS is typically used inside local networks, including in container networks in Kubernetes clusters and on build servers in development environments. However, it is also enabled on many embedded devices and in network-attached storage (NAS) devices which might be running older kernel versions and can only be patched with firmware updates. Tracked as CVE-2026-99362 and dubbed NFS2ROOT, the flaw affects systems running the NFSv4.1 or NFSv4.2 versions of the Network File System protocol, the default in many Linux distributions. The vulnerability allows anyone who can reach a server’s port 2049 to corrupt the memory of the nfsd process, the kernel component that serves NFS requests. It is rated 9.8 in severity. A researcher with French security agency ANSSI, Jérémy Jean, found the bug in August, and his fix was merged into the mainline kernel on September 14. According to security firm OpenSec Intelligence, which also discovered the heap overflow vulnerability and published technical details about it this week, the flaw can be exploited to gain a shell with root privileges. OpenSec found the bug using its AI-powered security testing harness and submitted its own patch to the Linux kernel maintainers on September 22. However, since it takes time for all supported kernel branches to backport fixes, the bug wasn’t disclosed, nor was a CVE ID assigned, until November 19. The flaw was introduced in Linux 3.16 in 2014 and is now patched in eight stable kernel branches: 5.10.275, 5.15.226, 6.1.193, 6.6.163, 6.12.117, 6.18.61, 7.3.2 and 7.4-rc1. On systems that can’t be immediately patched, administrators are advised to use firewall rules that block access to port 2049 from untrusted systems. Another option is to turn off NFSv4.1 and 4.2 in the nfsd config and then restart the service, but this will turn off pNFS and some features.

items.title: Ransomware Attacks Spike 23% in October with Recovery Taking Weeks
items.summary: A recent analysis of ransomware attacks has revealed that while the digital forensic investigation is often completed within 48 hours of an attack, the recovery typically takes several weeks for the majority of victims. The study was conducted by the Zero Labs team at the cybersecurity and data security company Rubrik between January 2026 and October 2026, and involved an analysis of internal telemetry, almost 17,000 publicly reported incidents, and real recovery cases where the victim sought help recovering from an attack. In 68% of analyzed attacks, the forensics findings took 48 hours or less; however, only one-third (32%) of attack victims made a full recovery within two weeks. For the majority of victims, it took several weeks to fully recover, and for 28% of victims it took longer than 6 weeks. The median recovery time was 20 days. From the analysis of 2,931 public incident reports, 45% explicitly stated that files had been encrypted, 67% of attacks confirmed data theft, and in 13% of attacks, encryption and data theft were confirmed. These figures represent minimum percentages, as they are based on what the threat actor chose to disclose. In many cases, threat actors often publicly disclose when data has been stolen to pressure victims into paying the ransom but fail to state if files were also encrypted. In the vast majority of incidents (94%), the method of initial access was not disclosed. Out of the 6% of incidents where the method of initial access was disclosed, more than half – 54% – involved the exploitation of an unpatched vulnerability. In 18% of attacks, initial access was gained using compromised credentials, 14% involved phishing or other malicious emails, 7% involved automated AI attacks, and 4% involved supply chain compromise. Given the extent to which vulnerabilities are being exploited for initial access, ensuring patches are applied promptly on Internet-facing assets should be the priority. Rubrik recommends tracking time-to-patch of internet-facing assets and making it a board-level measure, and ensuring that phishing-resistant MFA is enforced. Rubrik said that in at least 7% of recovery cases, the ransomware group attempted to log in to the victim’s backup management console, although that figure could be as high as 14%. The ransomware groups that dominate public reporting are the ones that typically reach backup environments, and in those cases, recovery often takes several weeks. Based on its analysis, 21% of ransomware groups were identified in customers’ backup environments, as attackers are increasingly targeting the systems that organizations rely on to recover, thereby increasing the probability that they will pay the ransom to recover their data. Healthcare victims topped the list in public reports and recovery cases, accounting for 26% and 23% of victims, respectively. The most active groups targeting the healthcare sector based on public reports were Nightspire (25%), Inc Ransom (23%), The Gentlemen (23%), LockBit (23%), SafePay (22%), and Qilin (18%). Quarterly reports issued by several cybersecurity firms show that ransomware attacks are increasing. A recent analysis of ransomware attacks by the cybersecurity and risk mitigation company NCC Group identified 1,049 incidents claimed by ransomware groups in October, an increase of 23% from September. NCC Group reports that Q3 2026 saw the highest quarterly volume of claimed attacks since NCC Group has been tracking ransomware attack claims. The increase in attacks has been attributed to attackers’ use of AI tools to identify and exploit vulnerabilities. NCC Group found that industrials was the sector most heavily targeted, accounting for 31% of claimed attacks. Healthcare ranked third, accounting for 12% of claimed attacks.

items.title: Critical Drupal Security Flaw Leads to Site Takeover Attacks
items.summary: Drupal Security Vulnerability Drupal has identified a critical vulnerability that enables unauthorized individuals to seize control of websites running the content management system. Recent Exploits The security team at Drupal reports that malicious actors are actively exploiting this weakness, which represents the second significant security flaw to be compromised in recent weeks. Previous Vulnerability Prior to this discovery, Drupal addressed a remote code execution vulnerability, cataloged as CVE-2026-132165 and known as Fail2Install. This issue permitted any anonymous user to take over a website by manipulating the Drupal installation process. Although the initial security notification did not indicate active exploitation, a subsequent update revealed that malicious actors began targeting the vulnerability within a day of the patch’s release. New Vulnerability Details The newly identified vulnerability, CVE-2026-136716, was remediated one week after the first patch. This flaw addresses additional attack vectors that were not resolved by the previous fix and similarly allows for the complete hijacking of vulnerable Drupal websites. According to an official statement from Drupal, certain installations that are not fully or correctly configured remain susceptible to takeover, even in production environments. The compromised state of a website is not readily apparent through the standard user interface, and websites that have already been infiltrated may no longer exhibit the vulnerable conditions. Recommended Actions Drupal has confirmed that this vulnerability is being exploited in real-world attacks. The organization has advised any website operator who may have left its installation files accessible following the initial security advisory to assume their site may have been compromised. Administrators are instructed to verify that the primary user account, designated as user 1, is under their control and to consider resetting its credentials. A thorough review of system logs for any unauthorized activity is recommended, with a specific focus on any unexpected modifications associated with the user 1 account. If signs of a breach are detected, administrators should follow the remediation guidance provided by Drupal. Temporary Mitigation For organizations unable to immediately upgrade to the latest versions of Drupal—specifically 10.6.23, 11.3.23, or 11.4.14—the recommended mitigation is to secure the installation files. This can be achieved by blocking public access to the `/core/install.php` file through the web server’s configuration or by modifying the `.htaccess` file in the web root directory. Broader Security Trend This recent exploitation contributes to a broader trend of targeted attacks against Drupal. The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has documented six security vulnerabilities in Drupal that have been actively exploited in the wild since November 2021. Notably, two of these previously compromised flaws have also been leveraged in ransomware campaigns.

items.title: Fake Car Diagnostic Tools on GitHub Distribute Malware to Repair Shops
items.summary: Cybercriminals have established a new threat vector by distributing malicious software through fake automotive diagnostic tool repositories on GitHub. Main Threat Overview Researchers have identified at least 16 fraudulent projects that emerged within a two-week period in early November 2026. These deceptive repositories mimic legitimate automotive diagnostic software from manufacturers in Europe, North America, and Asia, as well as aftermarket repair tools and Electronic Control Unit programming utilities. Deception Strategy The attack campaign employs a sophisticated multi-layered deception strategy. Each fraudulent repository contains authentic open-source automotive components, including Controller Area Network files and Unified Diagnostic Services libraries. To enhance discoverability, the projects feature AI-generated README files optimized with automotive repair-related search terms to improve search engine rankings. Malware Delivery Process The actual malware payload is delivered through a multi-stage process. Users are instructed to execute a setup script that downloads a malicious package archive. This archive contains a compromised package.json file that points to a malicious index.js. When executed, this script initiates a download of a malicious executable. A secondary component, a counterfeit 404.html page designed to mimic GitHub’s loading screen, contains obfuscated JavaScript that redirects users to a remote server for final malware delivery. Target Impact The primary targets are automotive technicians and repair shop personnel. These systems are particularly valuable to attackers because they often maintain persistent access to manufacturer portals, storing credentials, session cookies, single sign-on tokens, and digital certificates. Stolen session tokens enable attackers to bypass authentication mechanisms and gain unauthorized access to sensitive systems including vehicle identification number histories, warranty information, and connected vehicle platforms. Current Situation and Recommendations This campaign represents an exploitation of trust in public code repositories, specifically targeting the automotive sector. While no confirmed system compromises have been reported, the potential impact is significant due to the high-value nature of the targeted systems. GitHub has removed the identified repositories following researcher notification. Security experts are advising technicians to exercise caution when installing diagnostic software from public repositories and to avoid executing scripts from untrusted sources.

items.title: Game Mining vs Real Crypto Mining: Key Differences
items.summary: Crypto gaming platforms present an alternative method for earning digital assets, simulating cryptocurrency mining through interactive gameplay rather than relying on physical hardware. Crypto Gaming Platforms Fundamental Distinction The fundamental distinction between conventional mining and game-based mining lies in the source of rewards. Traditional cryptocurrency mining involves using specialized equipment to solve complex mathematical puzzles that validate transactions on a blockchain network. Miners receive network incentives, such as newly minted coins or transaction fees, in exchange for this computational work. This process demands significant investment in hardware, substantial electrical power, and technical expertise. In contrast, crypto mining games simulate this process entirely within a software environment. Rewards are generated by the platform itself, funded through advertising revenue and in-game purchases rather than through direct blockchain participation. Example: RollerCoin A prominent example of this model is RollerCoin, a browser-based application launched in 2018. The game allows users to construct virtual mining operations. Players acquire digital miners to increase their “hash power,” which determines their earning potential. Hash power can be enhanced by completing various mini-games, including reaction-based challenges, puzzles, and arcade-style activities. Alternatively, users can spend in-game currency to purchase and upgrade their digital mining equipment. Earnings are distributed in multiple cryptocurrencies, and users can withdraw their funds after meeting the platform’s minimum threshold. Appeal and Accessibility The primary appeal of these games is their low barrier to entry. Participants are not required to purchase expensive mining hardware, nor do they face the physical constraints such as excessive heat, noise, or high electricity consumption. For newcomers to the cryptocurrency space, these games can serve as an educational tool, allowing users to become familiar with core concepts like digital wallets, withdrawal processes, cryptocurrency nomenclature, and the relationship between computational power and rewards. Financial Viability and Considerations However, the financial viability of crypto mining games is often limited. Earnings from free gameplay are typically minimal. Achieving substantial rewards usually demands either a significant time investment or direct financial contributions to the platform. Several factors should be carefully considered before participating. The hourly return rate for free play is generally far below standard minimum wages. Furthermore, while in-game purchases can accelerate progress, spending money to earn small returns is rarely a profitable strategy. Users are also subject to platform-specific risks, as their account balances are contingent on the platform’s continued operation and adherence to its terms of service. Additionally, withdrawal processes may involve minimum balance requirements and associated fees. Educational Value Despite the modest financial returns, these games do offer educational value by providing a practical, interactive introduction to the mechanics of cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. The experience of managing digital assets and understanding reward structures can be beneficial for those new to the ecosystem. Conclusion In summary, crypto mining games do not constitute actual cryptocurrency mining and should not be viewed as a reliable path to significant income. They function as an accessible entry point into the world of digital assets, offering an entertaining way for users to learn about blockchain concepts while potentially earning small amounts of cryptocurrency. The games are best approached as a recreational activity with a crypto bonus rather than a primary source of income. If participation is based solely on financial gain, expectations should remain grounded in reality.

The fundamental distinction between conventional mining and game-based mining lies in the source of rewards. Traditional cryptocurrency mining involves using specialized equipment to solve complex mathematical puzzles that validate transactions on a blockchain network. Miners receive network incentives, such as newly minted coins or transaction fees, in exchange for this computational work. This process demands significant investment in hardware, substantial electrical power, and technical expertise. In contrast, crypto mining games simulate this process entirely within a software environment. Rewards are generated by the platform itself, funded through advertising revenue and in-game purchases rather than through direct blockchain participation.

Example: RollerCoin

A prominent example of this model is RollerCoin, a browser-based application launched in 2018. The game allows users to construct virtual mining operations. Players acquire digital miners to increase their “hash power,” which determines their earning potential. Hash power can be enhanced by completing various mini-games, including reaction-based challenges, puzzles, and arcade-style activities. Alternatively, users can spend in-game currency to purchase and upgrade their digital mining equipment. Earnings are distributed in multiple cryptocurrencies, and users can withdraw their funds after meeting the platform’s minimum threshold.

Appeal and Accessibility

The primary appeal of these games is their low barrier to entry. Participants are not required to purchase expensive mining hardware, nor do they face the physical constraints such as excessive heat, noise, or high electricity consumption. For newcomers to the cryptocurrency space, these games can serve as an educational tool, allowing users to become familiar with core concepts like digital wallets, withdrawal processes, cryptocurrency nomenclature, and the relationship between computational power and rewards.

Financial Viability and Considerations

However, the financial viability of crypto mining games is often limited. Earnings from free gameplay are typically minimal. Achieving substantial rewards usually demands either a significant time investment or direct financial contributions to the platform. Several factors should be carefully considered before participating. The hourly return rate for free play is generally far below standard minimum wages. Furthermore, while in-game purchases can accelerate progress, spending money to earn small returns is rarely a profitable strategy. Users are also subject to platform-specific risks, as their account balances are contingent on the platform’s continued operation and adherence to its terms of service. Additionally, withdrawal processes may involve minimum balance requirements and associated fees.

Educational Value

Despite the modest financial returns, these games do offer educational value by providing a practical, interactive introduction to the mechanics of cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. The experience of managing digital assets and understanding reward structures can be beneficial for those new to the ecosystem.

Conclusion

In summary, crypto mining games do not constitute actual cryptocurrency mining and should not be viewed as a reliable path to significant income. They function as an accessible entry point into the world of digital assets, offering an entertaining way for users to learn about blockchain concepts while potentially earning small amounts of cryptocurrency. The games are best approached as a recreational activity with a crypto bonus rather than a primary source of income. If participation is based solely on financial gain, expectations should remain grounded in reality.

OCR, the primary enforcer of HIPAA compliance, announced one enforcement action in September. A settlement was agreed with Ambry Genetics Corporation to resolve alleged noncompliance with multiple provisions of the HIPAA Security Rule. Ambry Genetics Corporation, a clinical genetic testing and genomics company, reported a breach of the unsecured protected health information (ePHI) of 225,370 individuals to OCR in March 2020. A malicious actor gained access to an email account after an employee responded to a phishing email. The exposed information included names, addresses, dates of birth, driver’s license numbers, diagnosis/condition information, medications, treatment information, and Social Security numbers.

OCR’s investigation determined that Ambry Genetics failed to conduct an accurate and thorough risk analysis to identify risks and vulnerabilities to ePHI, failed to implement policies and procedures for terminating access to ePHI after employment was terminated or access was no longer required, and unique usernames had not been assigned to all employees to allow their interactions with ePHI to be tracked. The alleged HIPAA violations were resolved with a $700,000 financial penalty and a corrective action plan to address the noncompliance issues.

State attorneys general also have the authority to investigate HIPAA-regulated entities and impose financial penalties for HIPAA violations. State attorneys general often join forces to investigate potential HIPAA violations, as was the case with the single penalty announced in September. A coalition of 44 attorneys general participated in a joint action against LabCorp, a North Carolina-based life sciences and healthcare company that provides clinical laboratory diagnostics and drug development services.

The case was settled with a $2,287,455 financial penalty, divided between the 44 participating states.

items.title: Air Force Cloud One Breach: Updates Blocked, Migration Paused, Scope Unknown
items.summary: Reuters reports a breach of the US Air Force’s Cloud One. The scope, attackers and data stolen remain unknown; updates are blocked. Reuters reports that hackers have breached Cloud One, one of the US Air Force ‘s main cloud computing platforms. The breach could put a large amount of sensitive military data at risk, including information about military operations, personnel, and logistics. Two sources said the intrusion was discovered about a month ago during work to upgrade the platform. The discovery has disrupted the entire service. Reuters could not identify the attackers, determine how much of the platform was affected, or confirm whether any data had been stolen. “Hackers have breached the US Air Force’s flagship cloud computing platform, three people familiar with the matter told ​Reuters, in a development that could jeopardize a vast swathe of sensitive tactical, personnel and logistics data.” Reuters states . “does not comment on the ​security posture, vulnerabilities or operational status of specific networks and systems.” reads a statement sent to Reuters by the Air Force. “We continuously take prudent measures to protect Department (of the Air Force) information, systems ​and mission capabilities.” Cloud One started in 2017 as a one-stop shop for the Air Force’s IT needs. It combines the resources of four operators, Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle and Alphabet, to run scores of applications, including ones for personnel data, pay, logistics and maintenance. Two of the sources say it’s among the military’s biggest cloud platforms. Two applications show why the breach is serious. Cloud-Based Command and Control brings together air defense radar data and other information from across North America. The Theater Integrated Combat Munitions System tracks bombs and missiles at more than 200 US Air Force locations worldwide. SAIC was the main contractor until 2025, when Leidos took over. SAIC did not respond to Reuters, while Leidos referred questions to the Air Force. According to one source, investigators have asked US Cyber Command, the military’s cyber unit, to assess the damage. Cyber Command did not respond to Reuters either. “A breach here is a big deal,” one of the sources told Reuters. The disruption is already visible. Two sources, plus a fourth person familiar with the matter, say efforts to migrate back-office applications to Cloud One, a longstanding military priority, have been paused. A fifth source says some users had their administrator rights revoked. The timing makes the incident more serious. Updates to applications running on Cloud One were blocked, leaving Air Force personnel unable to install fixes. This happened just as several serious software vulnerabilities were being disclosed across the technology industry. All five sources spoke to Reuters on condition of anonymity. According to one source, the attackers exploited a software flaw to access the platform’s control plane, which manages its main functions. The source compared it to a universal remote control. “Updates to applications already running on Cloud One were blocked, leaving Air Force personnel unable to apply fixes just as a new batch of serious software vulnerabilities has been disclosed across the technology industry.” Reuters continues. “A fifth source said that some users had their administrator rights revoked.” The breach lands amid heightened anxiety over AI-powered intrusions. Cloud networks are a particular worry because AI models can swiftly detect weaknesses across wide surface areas. The US government is already dealing with at least six other recently disclosed incidents, including two at the FBI, a previous hack of Pentagon data, a leak of Department of Homeland Security personnel information, a breach affecting at least two spy agencies and a hack at the Treasury Department. items.title: CISA Adds Three Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
items.summary: CISA has added three new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog , based on evidence of active exploitation. CVE-2026-120705 OSGeo GeoServer XML Injection Vulnerability CVE-2026-129243 OSGeo GeoServer Incorrect Authorization Vulnerability CVE-2026-136716 Drupal Core Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions Vulnerability These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise. Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities . CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria . Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form . Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.

items.title: SAP Security Incident: Stolen Tokens Raise Supply Chain Concerns
items.summary: SAP confirms a security incident as reports point to stolen GitHub tokens and altered source code. Data breach remains unconfirmed. SAP has confirmed a security incident, and most of the details come from the press, not from the company. The global enterprise found suspicious activity in its IT systems. DER SPIEGEL reported that attackers stole company employees’ access tokens and used them to change and copy source code on GitHub. “According to information obtained by SPIEGEL, the software manufacturer SAP is now dealing with an incident. The perpetrators may have used AI systems for assistance.” reads the report published by DER SPIEGEL. The German software maker says it took immediate steps to protect customers and secure its services. SAP says investigators had found no evidence of unauthorized access to customer business data at that stage. It didn’t answer detailed questions about the incident. An internal memo cited by Spiegel calls the incident active, and SAP is reportedly handling the investigation under the name “Project Granite”. Sources inside the software giant also told Spiegel that the attackers may have used AI agents. SAP has not confirmed this, and it is still unclear whether AI played any role in the attack. For now, this should be treated as an unconfirmed report. Employees were reportedly told not to discuss the incident. The report also says SAP management does not believe it needs to inform customers proactively. SAP reportedly told German broadcaster Tagesschau that customer data was not affected. SAP has not disclosed how the attackers obtained the employees’ tokens. Cybersecurity News recently reported a separate case in which a malicious VS Code extension stole GitHub tokens, but there is no evidence linking that attack to the SAP incident. SAP publishes source code for its products and open-source projects on GitHub. However, the report does not say which repositories were affected or whether the stolen code was public or private. This information is important to understand the impact of the incident. GitHub’s audit log guidance explains how organizations can trace recorded actions back to a compromised token, and administrators can revoke credentials by user and token type. items.title: One-Click Tor Browser Exploit Leaked Users’ Real IP; the Deeper Gap Closed Only in October
items.summary: A malicious website could learn the real IP address of a Tor Browser user after a single click, security firm Calif showed on 26 November. Calif’s write-up attacks Tor Browser 15.0.22 on default settings, a version that was current for about a week in September. Calif says the chain stopped working with 15.0.23. The current version is 16.0.3, out since 24 November. What Calif doesn’t spell out is what that patch covered. We went through Mozilla’s advisories and its public source code. The September update fixed the memory bug the chain starts with. As far as the public code shows, the step that let a hacked page borrow the browser’s highest privileges was closed only on 22 October, and it reached Tor Browser with version 16.0 a week later. Tor Browser 15.0, the last version for 32-bit Linux and older Android phones, never got that second change. Security news sites such as Cybernews have reported the research since, mostly repeating that 15.0.23 fixed it.

items.title: Flight Centre Cyber Breach: Customer Data Potentially Accessed
items.summary: Flight Centre Travel Group Cybersecurity Incident Flight Centre Travel Group is addressing a cybersecurity incident involving a third-party accommodation booking platform that may have exposed customer records including passport details, contact information, and in some cases sensitive health data. Incident Overview The company publicly acknowledged the breach on November 26, 2026, after identifying unauthorized activity within a system used by multiple travel brands including Flight Centre, Travel Associates, Cruiseabout, and various independent travel agents. Investigation and Response Following the detection of suspicious activity in the externally supplied booking platform, Brisbane-based Flight Centre initiated an investigation with cybersecurity experts and the technology vendor. The ongoing investigation aims to determine how unauthorized access was achieved, identify compromised information, and establish if customer data was extracted by intruders. Flight Centre has not revealed the name of the third-party service provider or the precise number of customers potentially impacted. Initial findings indicate unauthorized entities may have accessed a significant quantity of customer records, though the complete scope is not yet known. Compromised Information The types of potentially exposed information vary among affected records. Most compromised entries contain customer names and in some cases fundamental travel details. A smaller subset may include partial passport information, addresses, telephone numbers, and dates of birth. In isolated instances, health or mobility-related data may have been accessed, which is particularly sensitive as it pertains to personal circumstances and travel requirements. What Was Not Compromised The company has stated its investigators found no indication that customers’ credit card, payment, or banking account information was accessed. Flight Centre confirmed flight and corporate travel bookings remain unaffected as corporate services operate on separate systems and leisure travel functions continue normally. Customer Advisory Customers with existing accommodation reservations can proceed with planned travel, though the company urges caution regarding unexpected communications about bookings. Following the discovery, Flight Centre enacted cybersecurity response protocols, contained unauthorized activity, replaced authentication credentials, and heightened monitoring of the compromised environment. Potential Risks Although financial data wasn’t compromised, exposed personal and travel details could be misused for phishing campaigns, identity fraud, and targeted impersonation. Criminals with traveler itinerary information could pose as airline representatives, accommodation providers, or travel agents requesting additional payments or claiming reservations need immediate confirmation. Flight Centre has advised customers to verify unexpected communications through established official contact channels and refrain from sharing passwords, payment information, or personal details in response to unsolicited requests. Current Status and Future Actions The company continues its investigation and has begun notifying affected customers directly. The identity of responsible parties and the specific method used to gain unauthorized access haven’t been publicly disclosed. This incident raises broader questions about security of customer data managed by external technology providers. Flight Centre previously faced regulatory scrutiny following an unrelated data disclosure in 2017 involving approximately 6,918 customers. Under Australia’s data breach notification legislation, incidents creating likelihood of serious harm must be reported to relevant privacy regulators and affected individuals.

items.title: Retired CAG Officer Scammed in Canara Bank Pension Card Fraud, Lakhs Lost
items.summary: An elderly retired official from the Comptroller and Auditor General’s office in Mumbai fell victim to a financial scam, losing ₹5.56 lakh through a fraudulent Canara Bank pension card scheme. Victim Details The incident targeted Pandurang Dhopeshwarkar, an 89-year-old former CAG officer residing in Mulund East, Mumbai. Having retired in 1995, Dhopeshwarkar lives with his 80-year-old wife. The Scam Unfolds The fraudulent activity commenced at approximately 11:15 AM on November 25 when he received a call from an unknown number. The caller purported to be from Canara Bank and offered him a senior citizen card, which Dhopeshwarkar declined. Minutes later, a second call came through, this time from a different number that displayed the Canara Bank logo. The caller presented a new card, promising medical and railway travel benefits, framing it as a specialized banking service for senior citizens. During this conversation, Dhopeshwarkar received a file named “CANARA PENSION CARD UPDATE APK.” Trusting the communication due to the displayed bank logo, he attempted to open the file on his mobile device. The file failed to open, leading him to end the call. Financial Loss Within five to ten minutes, Dhopeshwarkar started receiving notifications of debit transactions on his bank-linked mobile number. Five unauthorized Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions were processed, resulting in a total loss of ₹5,56,626. The funds were illicitly transferred from his Canara Bank pension and savings accounts. Aftermath Upon discovering the unauthorized withdrawals, Dhopeshwarkar reported the incident via the national cybercrime helpline, 1930. He subsequently filed a formal complaint at the Navghar police station in Mumbai. This case involves a banking impersonation fraud where unidentified individuals used the bank’s name and logo to establish trust before delivering a malicious APK file. This incident underscores the dangers associated with unsolicited banking communications and suspicious files shared through messaging applications.

items.title: Flight Centre Data Breach: Passport Details Compromised
items.summary: Flight Centre Travel Group Customer Data Breach The Brisbane-based travel company Flight Centre Travel Group (FLT) has reported a customer data breach affecting customers who booked accommodations through its Flight Centre brand, Travel Associates, Cruiseabout, and several independent agents. Breach Details The breach, which does not impact flight bookings or corporate travel reservations, was discovered in a third-party accommodation booking system. According to a statement filed with the Australian Securities Exchange, the company is investigating suspicious activity within the compromised system. While investigations are ongoing, FLT suspects that a substantial volume of customer records may have been accessed by unauthorized individuals, though the exact number of records extracted remains undetermined. Data Accessed An initial assessment of the incident indicates that the majority of compromised records contain only customer names, often accompanied by basic travel itinerary details. A small subset of the accessed data is believed to include more sensitive information such as limited passport details, residential addresses, telephone numbers, dates of birth, and in rare instances, health or mobility-related data. The company has confirmed that no customer credit card, payment, or bank account information was accessed. Mitigation Measures To mitigate the breach, FLT has engaged its cybersecurity incident response partner, Mandiant, and is working with the system vendor to implement containment measures and appropriate safeguards. The company has taken immediate action to contain the incident by changing authentication keys and credentials, enhancing system monitoring, and notifying relevant authorities. Customer Response Flight Centre Travel Group has emphasized its commitment to customer privacy and data security, acknowledging the unsettling nature of the incident for potentially affected customers and offering an apology for any concern caused. The company has advised customers to remain vigilant against potential phishing attempts, urging them to avoid clicking on suspicious links, opening unexpected attachments, or sharing personal information, passwords, or payment details in response to unsolicited communications. Industry Context This incident is part of a recent trend of breaches within the travel industry. In April, the online travel platform Booking.com disclosed a breach affecting customer reservation data, including names, addresses, and information shared with accommodations. Similarly, in late October, accommodation software provider RMS Cloud, which serves over 6,000 hotels and holiday parks, confirmed a breach following reports of phishing attacks received by guests of several Australian holiday park operators.

items.title: Microsoft Emergency Hotpatch Fixes Windows Server Crashes
items.summary: Microsoft has deployed an unscheduled patch to resolve critical failures impacting Windows Server 2025 systems. Emergency Update for Windows Server 2025 Microsoft has deployed an unscheduled patch to resolve critical failures impacting Windows Server 2025 systems. The out-of-band update, designated KB5138318, specifically addresses stop errors characterized by code 0x139 that occur when IPv6 route timers expire on servers with Router Advertisement functionality enabled. Problem Details According to Microsoft, the problem manifests exclusively on certain Windows Server 2025 installations following the application of the November 2026 security hotpatch, identified as KB5131077. The company explained that affected machines may experience unexpected termination with the KERNEL_SECURITY_CHECK_FAILURE error under specific network conditions. Update Distribution The emergency non-security update is being distributed through Windows Update to eligible Windows Server 2025 devices participating in the hotpatch program. Recent Update Issues The release follows a series of recent update-related issues affecting multiple Microsoft platforms. Concurrently, Windows 11 users are reporting complications with the November 2026 hotpatch, including installation and execution failures for Office and third-party applications, alongside printing malfunctions on systems equipped with Forcepoint’s DLP Endpoint Agent. Hotpatch Technology Implementation Microsoft’s hotpatch technology, which reached general availability in July 2022 following a public preview that commenced in June of that year, is undergoing broader implementation. The company announced in March 2026 that it would enable hotpatch updates by default for all compatible Windows devices managed via Microsoft Graph API or Microsoft Intune, a policy effective after the May 2026 security updates. Previous Hotpatch Deployment Issue This rollout followed the resolution in June 2025 of a Windows Autopatch issue that inappropriately deployed driver updates on some Autopatch-managed systems in the European Union, bypassing administrative restrictions.

items.title: Colorado Data Breach Impacts 100,000 Residents
items.summary: The Colorado Governor’s Office of Information Technology has revealed a security incident that exposed user data within the myColorado mobile application. Security Incident in myColorado Mobile Application The Colorado Governor’s Office of Information Technology has revealed a security incident that exposed user data within the myColorado mobile application. This official state platform provides digital identification, access to government services, and document storage capabilities, serving approximately 2.1 million residents. Immediate Response and Investigation Following the detection of unauthorized access, state officials immediately took the application offline and launched an investigation. The intrusion was discovered after the attackers triggered automated threat detection mechanisms operating within the application’s Amazon Web Services environment. The security team initiated response protocols upon identifying the breach. Compromised Data and Impact The compromised data stems from the ‘myCards and Documents’ feature, where users upload personal files. This includes scanned copies of government-issued identification documents, vehicle registration certificates, and insurance cards. The investigation indicates that approximately 100,000 individuals may have been affected by the incident. Authorities have confirmed that no financial payment information was accessed during the breach. Ongoing Response and Notifications State personnel are currently working to correlate the improperly accessed documents with individual user accounts. As this matching process continues, officials expect to refine the estimated number of impacted individuals. The application remains offline, and no timeline for its restoration has been provided. The state anticipates beginning direct notifications to affected users on November 27. Focus on User Protection The primary focus of the response remains user protection and system restoration with enhanced security measures. “Our main goal is to protect the security of users. Additionally, we are prioritizing direct notification of users involved in the incident and getting the app up and running as soon as possible, with security enhancements in place,” stated Sarah Tuneberg, the state’s Chief Information Officer and executive director of the Office of Information Technology. items.title: SAP Cyberattack Confirmed: Source Code Compromised in Data Breach
items.summary: SAP has acknowledged a cybersecurity incident impacting its development environment. SAP Confirms Cybersecurity Incident Enterprise software developer SAP has acknowledged a cybersecurity incident impacting its development environment. The confirmation follows reports from German media indicating that malicious actors targeted the company’s internal infrastructure. According to SAP, the organization identified suspicious activity and has taken immediate steps to safeguard its services and protect customer interests. The company stated that its investigation has not uncovered any indication that customer business data was accessed without authorization. SAP declined to provide specific details regarding the attack’s nature or origin. Attack Details Internal communications reviewed by the German press reveal that the suspicious activity was detected within GitHub, a platform where SAP hosts developer tools, sample applications, and open-source projects. An insider source claims that attackers acquired authentication tokens belonging to SAP employees, which enabled them to access and modify source code stored on the platform. It remains undetermined if any proprietary code was compromised. Response and Impact In response to the incident, SAP has reportedly implemented emergency security measures that have impacted multiple teams within the organization. These actions include replacing cryptographic signing keys, restricting access to GitHub repositories, and suspending automated development workflows. There is no indication that any tampered code was deployed to customers as a result of the breach. AI Involvement and Other Incidents The possibility of artificial intelligence being involved in the attack has been raised, though this has not been substantiated. The emergence of AI-assisted cyberattacks has been noted by several major organizations in recent months. In late October, the ransomware group known as Gentlemen listed SAP on its leak site, suggesting a compromise of the company’s Latin American operations. However, file listings indicate the data pertained to software and source code from a third party, and the two incidents do not appear to be related.

items.title: Linux NFS2ROOT Vulnerability: Critical Flaw Allows Root Privilege Escalation
items.summary: A critical vulnerability in the Linux kernel’s Network File System server, designated CVE-2026-99362, has been identified that permits unauthenticated remote attackers to obtain root privileges. NFS2ROOT Vulnerability Details The issue, which has persisted for 12 years, was discovered by J r my Jean of ANSSI, who submitted a remedy in August. OpenSec, a cybersecurity firm, has named the flaw NFS2ROOT and provided a complete remote-root exploit along with a patch to the NFSD maintainers by late September. Vulnerability Impact The vulnerability traces back to Linux kernel version 3.16, released in March 2014, and originates from a heap buffer overflow within the Linux NFS server (nfsd). Systems running a kernel older than 6.12.117, 6.18.61, 7.3.2, or 7.4-rc1 are at risk if nfsd (versions 4.1 or 4.2) is active and TCP port 2049 is accessible from the internet. Successful exploitation enables unprivileged remote actors to corrupt kernel memory and achieve root access through low-complexity attacks that do not require user interaction. Attack Mechanism The NFS2ROOT attack sequence involves sending maliciously crafted requests to the NFS server, causing it to write data outside the bounds of an allocated memory buffer. This allows attackers to read kernel memory, circumvent KASLR (Kernel Address Space Layout Randomization), and implant a callback that executes a command in a freed memory region. Upon closing the NFS connection, the kernel executes the embedded command with elevated privileges, granting the attacker root control over the compromised server. Mitigation Recommendations Although there are no documented instances of CVE-2026-99362 being actively exploited in the wild, security personnel are urged to immediately apply the latest kernel security updates from their Linux distribution vendor and reboot the system to ensure the patched kernel is active. Organizations unable to patch immediately should restrict access to the NFS server on TCP port 2049 to trusted clients or networks. Furthermore, if NFS functionality is not required, administrators can stop and disable the nfs-server service in /etc/nfs.conf. Expert Analysis OpenSec emphasized that port 2049 is exposed on file servers, NAS appliances, build farms, and Kubernetes storage nodes, and since 2014, the Linux kernel listening on this port has permitted anyone who can reach it to write into kernel memory without authentication. They stated that kernel hardening does not resolve the overflow and that every host must be patched. Detection Methods While NFS2ROOT attacks lack network signatures, security teams can monitor for potential exploitation indicators by looking for kernel warnings from nfsd4_check_resp_size, shells spawned by kernel workers on file servers, bursts of short NFSv4.1 sessions originating from a single source, and kernel oopses involving nfsd4_*, svc_*, or call_usermodehelper* frames. A critical vulnerability in the Linux kernel’s Network File System server, designated CVE-2026-99362, has been identified that permits unauthenticated remote attackers to obtain root privileges.

NFS2ROOT Vulnerability Details

The issue, which has persisted for 12 years, was discovered by J r my Jean of ANSSI, who submitted a remedy in August. OpenSec, a cybersecurity firm, has named the flaw NFS2ROOT and provided a complete remote-root exploit along with a patch to the NFSD maintainers by late September.

Vulnerability Impact

The vulnerability traces back to Linux kernel version 3.16, released in March 2014, and originates from a heap buffer overflow within the Linux NFS server (nfsd). Systems running a kernel older than 6.12.117, 6.18.61, 7.3.2, or 7.4-rc1 are at risk if nfsd (versions 4.1 or 4.2) is active and TCP port 2049 is accessible from the internet. Successful exploitation enables unprivileged remote actors to corrupt kernel memory and achieve root access through low-complexity attacks that do not require user interaction.

Attack Mechanism

The NFS2ROOT attack sequence involves sending maliciously crafted requests to the NFS server, causing it to write data outside the bounds of an allocated memory buffer. This allows attackers to read kernel memory, circumvent KASLR (Kernel Address Space Layout Randomization), and implant a callback that executes a command in a freed memory region. items.title: FIFA Confirms a Cyberattack, Hackers Claim 12 GB of Internal Files
items.summary: FIFA confirms a cyberattack exposing personal and business data, while the Handsome Boy Hacking Club claims responsibility for the breach. FIFA confirmed it was the victim of a cyberattack, threat actors gained access to what soccer’s world governing body describes as a “limited set of personal and business information.” The organization told The Associated Press it’s working closely with the relevant authorities, including law enforcement. FIFA did not disclose technical details about the attack or what kind of information hackers accessed. A hacking group, which calls itself the Handsome Boy Hacking Club, claimed the security incident before FIFA made its announcement. The threat actors shared a screenshot on X showing what it claimed were FIFA files. Three days later, the group appeared to claim responsibility for the attack in a reply to a post reporting that more than 12 GB of FIFA internal documents had been leaked. FIFA has confirmed that hackers broke into its systems and accessed personal and business information. A new group calling itself Handsome Boy Hacking Club claims it took more than 12GB from FIFA's Microsoft environment, including identity and immigration documents, and… pic.twitter.com/ZwxJ7LoQez — International Cyber Digest (@IntCyberDigest) November 26, 2026 At this moment, the group’s X account has been suspended, and their Tor leak site is unreachable. “FIFA condemns in the strongest possible terms the unlawful acquisition and publication of information, particularly personal data,” states the organization. “Such actions constitute a serious and unacceptable violation of privacy and can have significant consequences for the individuals concerned.” The breach comes at a sensitive time for FIFA and its president, Gianni Infantino, who faces criticism over a failed plan to sell World Cup stakes to private investors and his bid to extend his presidency to 2031. He remains the favorite ahead of the March 18 election, against Kohzo Tashima and Philippe Diallo. The AP report does not link the cyberattack to these issues. FIFA warns that the exposure of personal data could have serious consequences for those affected. “Such actions constitute a serious and unacceptable violation of privacy and can have significant consequences for the individuals concerned.” concludes the AP. Handsome Boy Hacking Club (HBHC) is a newly emerged ransomware and data-extortion group first observed in November 2026. Threat intelligence platforms recorded its first activity on November 19, when it listed three organizations on its data-leak site: US-based firearms manufacturer Smith & Wesson, healthcare provider UCHealth, and telecommunications company Frontier Communications. On November 20, the group added FIFA to its victim list, bringing the number of publicly recorded claims to four. The group has provided little information about its operators, origins, or technical capabilities. Its claims involve organizations in the United States and Switzerland, spanning the manufacturing, healthcare, telecommunications, and sports sectors. While FIFA has confirmed a cyberattack resulting in unauthorized access to personal and business information, the other listings should be treated as claims that have not necessarily been independently verified. items.title: Zero Trust for AWS Landing Zones: A Complete Architecture Guide
items.summary: This blog is co-authored by Chamandeep Singh, Security Technology Leader - Partners, AWS. Picture the moment - you are deep in a cloud migration. You have spent months designing your AWS Landing Zone. Multi-account structure. Service Control Policies. Transit Gateway. Centralized logging. You followed every best-practice guide AWS published. It feels like the hard work is behind you. And in many ways, it is.But the architecture diagram does not answer one question: who inspects the traffic flowing between your workloads and the internet, enforces identity-aware policy at the point of connection, and does so across hundreds of accounts at line speed without deploying inspection infrastructure in every VPC? Two Classes of Control, Both EssentialAWS Landing Zones represent architectural maturity. A well-built Landing Zone gives you a multi-account structure enforced by AWS Organizations, guardrails through Service Control Policies, centralized security visibility via AWS Security Hub and Amazon GuardDuty, audit trails through AWS CloudTrail and Amazon CloudWatch, and a network topology, typically hub-and-spoke through AWS Transit Gateway, that gives you control over how traffic moves between accounts.That is a strong foundation, and Zscaler builds on that foundation by delivering real-time inline traffic inspection, identity-driven policy enforcement at the point of connection, and Zero Trust protection across the full hybrid estate. Together, they cover the complete picture. And at scale, both layers are essential.This requirement becomes more pressing as organizations adopt AI and machine learning workloads that call external APIs at high frequency, pull training data from distributed sources, and exchange inference results with downstream consumers. The volume of machine-to-machine traffic in a modern AWS environment can far exceed human user traffic. Security architectures designed around user access alone leave the majority of traffic unchecked. Why Legacy Patterns Fail at Cloud ScaleLegacy solutions on enterprise AWS environments do provide a certain level of protection. Organizations recognize the traffic risk and respond with what they know: virtual firewalls - the same network security appliances from their data centres, redeployed in the cloud. A rational starting point. But an architectural mismatch.Virtual firewalls were designed to enforce a perimeter. They inspect at the network layer, apply policy based on source IP and destination port, and assume a stable topology. Cloud environments are none of those things. Workloads scale dynamically, accounts multiply, and traffic patterns shift constantly. Managing rule sets at that pace, keeping HA pairs in sync, updating route tables, and writing policies for workloads that may exist for hours introduces operational complexity that grows faster than the environment it is trying to protect.The deeper problem is that the current attack patterns have moved. Modern attacks don't break through the perimeter; they authenticate through it. Compromised credentials, stolen tokens, and misconfigured access policies mean the threat is already inside the network, moving laterally from a session that looked legitimate at the edge. Frontier AI models are accelerating this pattern, enabling attackers to craft convincing credential theft campaigns at scale, automate reconnaissance across cloud environments, and move faster than detection-based controls can respond.Cloud-native environments require a different model - one built around identity and application context rather than network topology, and designed to enforce policy at the point of connection, not at a perimeter the modern evolving attack techniques have already learned to bypass. Two Pillars of Zero Trust for AWSThat model exists. Zscaler's Zero Trust Exchange, a cloud-native security platform that acts as a policy broker between users, workloads, and the applications they need to reach, integrates directly into the Landing Zone architecture, addressing both how users reach applications and how workloads communicate beyond the AWS boundary.Pillar 1: Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) - Zero Trust Access for UsersZscaler Private Access (ZPA) replaces VPN with a fundamentally different connectivity model. Rather than granting a user access to a network segment, ZPA brokers access to a specific application, for a specific user, evaluated against identity and device context, for the duration of that session only.The technical mechanism is an inside-out model. App Connectors are deployed in your centralized network VPC (or workload VPCs for a distributed topology) and establish outbound-only connections to the Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange. No inbound firewall rules are required. The application is never exposed to the internet - no public attack surface, no discoverable endpoint. When a user needs access, the Zero Trust Exchange brokers the connection after verifying identity and policy. If the policy check fails, there is no connection.
